articleTitle: Construction and investigation of the magnetrons for heating in industry and medicine
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The creation of new magnetrons having unusual values of f/sub 0/ and P/sub out/ will be successful if the main parameters of the geometry and mode of operation are correct. The frequency dependent impedance of the resonator system and emitting current giving stable output power generation are the most important parameters.

articleTitle: Problems of creation of powerful and super-power klystrons with efficiency up to 90%
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Discusses creation of cathodes with a high current density of emission, creation of three-dimensional election-optical systems with a high compression of electron beams and creation of spatially-developed multiresonator electrodynamic systems. The analysis of a possibility of creation of multibeam klystron with output power 80-100 MW and with power supply voltage rating no more than 120 kW in a range 12 MHz was conducted by Stanford University. The analysis has shown that the creation of such device is quite possible. Thus, the creation of high-power and super-power klystrons with rather low supply voltage and very high (up to 90%) efficiency is possible.

articleTitle: An S-band klystron with advanced features
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)

articleTitle: High energy microwave device research at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The primary purpose of microwave tube research and development at SLAC is the construction of very high energy density pulsed microwave sources to power future electron-positron colliders. In this paper, the SLAC work on very high power klystrons is reviewed, as is the development of improved output circuits to reduce RF gradients, the use of periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing in conjunction with multiple beams, and the research on cathodes and RF breakdown.

articleTitle: High-power broadband pulse multiple-beam klystrons with output from 100 kW up to 1000 kW with a bandwidth up to 12%
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: High-power transmitting devices of radar systems are required frequently to supply levels of pulse output power from a hundred up to thousand kilowatt and an average output power of the order of 10 kW. Moreover, the radar transmitters should be maximum broad bandwidth to satisfy the requirements of anti-jamming and electromagnetic compatibility. The common requirement for klystrons used in these transmitters is the requirement of a low level of feeding voltages (beam voltage and modulation voltage). Multiple-beam klystron (MBK) design, which is based on the fundamental mode operation of resonators, has good perspectives for application in high-power transmitters. Some results of the developments of high-power multiple-beam klystrons operating in the fundamental resonator mode executed per the last decade are considered in the this paper.

articleTitle: Studies on broadband output circuit of high power klystron
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Three types of broadband output circuit, including filter-loaded output circuit, double gap coupling cavity operating in overlapping mode, and filter loaded double gap coupling cavity, have been studied and applied to a practical broadband klystron. The microwave equivalent circuit for calculating impedance-frequency characteristics and the design method for determining circuit parameters are descibed in this paper. S-band klystrons with a filter-loaded circuit have a bandwidth of 7.5% at a power level of 1 MW. S- and L-band klystrons with overlapping mode double gap coupling cavity have a bandwidth of 7.5/spl sim/10% at a power level of 700 kW to 1 MW. S- and L-band multi-beam klystrons have a bandwidth of 7/spl sim/11% at a power level of 200 kW.

articleTitle: Multiple beam klystrons
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The advantages of multiple beam klystrons (MBK) for consumers are low operating voltage with high power and efficiency at wide instantaneous bandwidth. The features of MBK for designers are low individual beam perveance, together with low total electron stream resistance. That helps obtain the high electronic and circuit efficiency. At the same time MBKs have difficulties in design. Some remedies are indicated. In spite of these difficulties, the author produced very successful low-voltage long-life MBKs for radar and communications applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of gyrotron coaxial cavities with corrugated inner conductor based on the method of moments
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)

articleTitle: Generation of UHF oscillations in slowing down lines with magnetic insulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In leading laboratories of the world intensive research on powerful microwave generators with magnetic self-isolation (MILO) is being carried out. In the present work the results of calculation and theoretical analysis of MILO, designed and tested in the Institute of Electromagnetic Research (IEMR), are given.

articleTitle: X-band high-power broadband low-voltage multi-beam klystron amplifier with two-barrel design
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the development of an X-band pulse amplifying klystron with a power output level of about 15 kW in a 5% operating bandwidth on the basis of a multibarrel design.

articleTitle: Experimental study and numerical simulation of electron beam in gyrotron-type electron-optical systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The most widely used system of helical electron beam (HEB) formation for gyrotron applications includes a magnetron-injection gun (MIG) and magnetic compression region. In this system, it is necessary to take into account such specific phenomena as the reflection of electrons with large transverse velocities from magnetic mirror, the accumulation of the space charge in the trap between gun cathode and magnetic field plateau, the excitation of low-frequency "trap" oscillations, the electron bombardment of cathode surface. These phenomena have an effect on HEB quality and limit gyrotron parameters. In our paper, the results of experimental study and numerical simulation of physical processes accompanying HEB formation are summarized.

articleTitle: Research progress and advances on high power klystron
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: High power klystron is a very important microwave Vacuum device with high peak and average power, high gain and efficiency, high stability and long life time. It has wide application in many microwave electronic systems such as modern radar and communication system, particle accelerator TV broadcast, fusion plasma heating and industrial heating system: and also future beam energy weapon. Research progress on the theory, design and calculation of the interaction section and electron optics of klystron in Institute of Electronics, Chinese Academy of Science (IECAS) are presented in the paper. Technical advances on key parts of klystron are briefly given out. Typical high power klystron, broadband klystron and multi-beam klystron developed in IECAS will be described in the paper.

articleTitle: Medical application of slow electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The development and realization of microwave radiators, based on slow-wave structures (SWS) application, has shown that the application of slow electromagnetic waves is extremely promising in different areas of medicine. A novel family of RF applicators and microwave radiators is offered and designed. An artificial ear with antenna on coupled spirals and coagulating scalpels with coupled combs on metal and dielectric blades were developed. This paper, based on analysis of the physical properties of slow electromagnetic waves and the laws of electrodynamics, presents the main features of SWS-based applicators and radiators which enable new application of RF and microwaves in medicine.

articleTitle: Mechanism of microwave pulse shortening in the relativistic backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)

articleTitle: Development of 1-MW long-pulse/CW gyrotrons in 110-170 GHz frequency range
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The given paper represents the review of modern experimental results, design features and perspectives of "GYCOM" gyrotrons further development. 140 GHz and 110 GHz "GYCOM" gyrotrons are used as sources of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) of plasma on W7-AX stellarator, ASDEX upgrade tokamak (both IPP, Germany), DIII-D tokamak (General atomic, USA), TdeV tokamak (CCFM, Canada). 110-GHz gyrotrons are characterized with the power levels of /spl sim/900 kW for 2-s pulse length and 500 kW for 5-s pulse length. In 140-GHz gyrotron power levels of /spl sim/900 kW for 1-s pulse length, /spl sim/50 kW in 2-s pulses and /spl sim/550 kW 3-s pulses are available. In the first 170 GHz gyrotron experimental sample, developed for the ITER project, the power of 1 MW for 1-s pulse length and 500 kW in 5-s pulses was reached. At the same time, gyrotrons with 1 MIN output power and 50% efficiency in a CW regime should be developed according to request of lTER and programs of modernization for existing installations.

articleTitle: Geometrized theory of relativistic electron beams
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The geometrized theory of dense electron beams is the newest part of contemporary corpuscular optics which includes the problems of non-paraxial relativistic beams synthesis, the questions of approximate solution construction and geometrized beam equations numerical integration.

articleTitle: A radar with nanosecond sounding pulse
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: It is known that utilization of short sounding pulses for ranging and the detection of point targets against the background of interfering reflections, especially at small distances, allows one to substantially increase the target-to-background ratio, due to the reduced size of the resolving cell, and, thus, improve detection characteristics and accuracy of estimates for their parameters. The source of interfering reflections may be a diffuse surface, tropospheric inhomogeneities, meteorological objects, parts of extended targets, etc. In this paper a breadboard model of a radar with a nanosecond sounding pulse is presented.

articleTitle: Design of a rotating mode filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The solution of the electromagnetic field is given for the TE mode in infinite fan-shaped waveguides. The basic principle of a rotating mode filter with a fan-shaped waveguide is presented. The design method for the filter is discussed by a practical example. The good experiment results for the filter are achieved for TE/sub 03/ mode operation.

articleTitle: Application of the code ISFEL3D for three-dimensional RF structure calculations
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Computer simulation of electromagnetic structures in three dimensions is at present the usual way to obtain the most important information about the field distribution in the parts of microwave devices where measurements give incorrect results. The intent of this work is to show the kinds of calculations that are currently being performed in the frequency domain using the ISFEL3D, a set of finite-element codes developed for the computer-aided design of fully three-dimensional electromagnetic structures in the frequency domain.

articleTitle: The program for design of broadband klystron amplifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The special code for a broadband klystron amplifier is described. The main differences from other codes are in the design of circuits and in the service corresponding to the work in the wide frequency bands. The data are deduced about agreement between the results of this code employment and the other sources for three high power klystrons.

articleTitle: Miniature injection-locked CW-magnetrons for portable and satellite communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Miniature injection-locked CW-magnetrons are a possible alternative to TWTs or klystrons in such systems where coherency and narrow bandwidth are needed. These magnetrons offer compact size, high efficiency and long life. In some applications miniature magnetrons have advantages in comparison with transistor amplifiers. Magnetron design contains several novel and patented designs. High performance quality of magnetron subblocks has been achieved by using of vacuum and microelectronic technologies.

articleTitle: Klystron input circuit
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The klystron input device calculation is described and realized as a part of a klystron simulation program. It is based on a gap field analytical study, a realistic equivalent circuit, and an iterative procedure for beam loading and gap voltage evaluation. The results from using this program are in sufficient agreement with experiment results and aid the understanding of klystron input device properties control. Some design methods are indicated.

articleTitle: The tuning system of broadband klystron amplifier
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The modern computer technology does not work out the problem of broadband klystron amplifier design by itself. It needs for a good initial approach on the base of physical notions. To form a system of buncher cavity resonant frequencies and Q's, the problem of RF currents interaction in the drift spaces is especially important. This subject is considered in this paper and the remedies are determined for obtaining of a flat gain frequency response. At first the "skirtron" tuning system is used, then the second cavity is detuned down and a multiple-coupled network is formed near the first cavity. Some other possibilities are discussed.

articleTitle: The ring resonator use the the power packed klystrons for the accelerators of the industrial and therapeutic purposes
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Beginning with 1986 year the SR&PC "Toriy" produces the multi-beam klystrons (MBK) of packed design that are intended to use in the electron accelerator apparatus (EA) of the industrial and medical purposes. The distinctive features of these MBK are the low voltage and reverse focusing system with packed permanent magnets. The enumerated distinctive features predetermine the necessity to use a big number of the electron beams (40) and make impossible to employ the traditional toroidal resonators because of the substantial radial irregularity over the interaction gap field. So, the ring resonators (RR), which are the coiling wave-guide of the H- or II-like cross-section, are employed in the klystrons.

articleTitle: Field emitters with carbon containing coverages and based on carbon fibers: possibilities of creation and use in microwave electronics
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: High chemical inertness of carbon materials and their stability upon ion bombardment makes them attractive for vacuum microwave devices. However, high work function of carbon, as well as technological difficulties of pure coverage and ordered structure formation prevent the creation of carbon field emitters, Only few investigations are known where attempts to create emission sources made of carbon or carbon containing coverages were performed. The present work deals with field emitters covered with molecules of C/sub 60/ and emitters made from carbon fibers. The results showed that the regularities of carbon containing coverage formation by means of fullerene molecule adsorption. The expediency to form a distributed structure consisting of the small microcluster was shown to give stable emission under acceptable voltages. The possibility to create a single tip emitter covered by carbon was discovered. Such an emitter with micron diameter secured a current of more than 100 /spl mu/A under the operating voltage /spl sim/15 kV in static regime. The nonordered multi-tip field emitter based on carbon fiber was also realized.

articleTitle: Slow-wave structures application for liquid level monitoring
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Obtaining reliable measurements of liquid level is important at power generation stations, on vehicles, at chemical storage facilities, and in many industrial processes. In recent years radiowave methods for level measurement were developed using long line sensing elements. The accuracy and reliability of these measurements can be substantially improved by replacing the long line element with a section of a Slow-Wave Structure (SWS).

articleTitle: Formulation of quasi-chaotic wide-band microwave output in an externally controlled amplitrons
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: High-power sources of a broad-band microwave radiation are required in a number of applications, including thermonuclear research, non-equilibrium plasma chemistry, non-linear radar-location, communication technology, etc. Such radiation may be obtained in standard microwave devices randomized by introduction of a non-linear delayed feedback, or in beam-plasma systems. Earlier we reported on realization of a new method of high-power quasi-noise broad-band microwave generation-in an amplitron controlled with RF fields introduced into the cathode-end regions of the interaction space. In this paper a more detailed description of the technique is given together with recently obtained experimental data giving clues for better understanding of mechanisms of a multi-frequency signal generation in amplitron.

articleTitle: Volumetric integral equation for complex media
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Anisotropic, bianisotropic and chiral media or so-called complex or composite materials have caused growing interest in terms of their theoretical investigation and wide field of applications. There have been several publications on the development of the Surface Integral Equation Method (SIEM) for bianisotropic planar structures, including transmission lines on bianisotropic substrates. The impedance or admittance SIEM is suitable only for infinite or shielded substrates with coordinate forms. For non-coordinate media the most efficient method is the Volumetric Integral Equation Method (VIEM), which have been extended here for bianisotropic media.

articleTitle: Problems of combination of broad band and high efficiency of klystron
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The results of this research were applied to existing designs of cathode blocks, electron guns and resonators. It allows synthesizing klystrons with parameters considerably exceeding existing ones. So, a klystron with efficiency of about 80% in a band more than 6% was synthesized on the basis of existing designs. The klystron with efficiency 65% in frequency band more than 25% and output power of about 5 MW was also synthesized on the basis of the existing design. These parameters are not limiting. The combination of higher efficiency and broader band is possible.

articleTitle: Advances and problems of high power gyrotrons
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The paper reviews some problems of physical electronic of high power gyrotron and possible solution, results of calculation and experimental study of gyrotrons for fusion operating in a wide frequency range and at the 1 MW power level. Effects of beam potential depression and mode interaction (competition and cooperation) in gyrotrons, methods of mode selection including multibeam and complex cavity systems are presented. The dependence of gyrotron parameters on the beam current and magnetic field is analyzed. The experimental results are compared with the calculated data.

articleTitle: Broadband multibeam pulse klystrons of moderate output power with a special control electrode
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this paper the authors describe the design of a multibeam klystron with a double-gap output resonator and a three-coupled-resonator output system. A 15-beam electron gun was used. As a result an industrial sample of a klystron with a special control electrode operating at a voltage of no more than 3.8 kV was developed. The output pulse power was more than 25 kW and average power more than 1.5 kW. The band of amplification constituted not less than 2% at an amplification more than 40 dB. The klystron is packaged by a SmCo magnet system and is liquid cooled. Its mass is less than 8 kg.

articleTitle: Recent high power klystron status in KEK
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In KEK there are three big projects such as KEKB project, Japanese Hadron Facility (JHF) and Linear Collider project (JLC). All projects include the linear accelerator, high power klystrons are key issues to develop them. In KEKB project, 59 S-band high power pulse klystrons are used and now under the commissioning. These S-band tubes were developed from the previous 30-MW klystron and produced 50-60 MW. JHF is the future plan of KEK and had a 200-Mev proton linear accelerator. We are now developing a UHF klystron (frequency of 324 MHz, peak power of 3 MW and rf pulse duration pf 650 microseconds). In JLC we have been developing the X-band high power klystrons under the collaboration between KEK and BINP. Recently 2D and 3D MAGIC code enable us to design klystrons more realistically. This report describes those three kinds of klystron developments.

articleTitle: Coaxial slowing down structure for hybrid UHF amplifier of range 1-3 GHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The excitation by an electron beam of UHF oscillations in a coaxial slowing down transmission line with a comb on internal and external cylinders is considered. The analytical and numerical analysis of the received dispersion equation is carried out. The dependence of the gain on energy of an electron beam is investigated. It is shown, that the dependence of the gain on frequency has a maximum nearby the Cherenkov resonance of a beam with an eigen wave structure. Outside of a resonance the gain falls down under the linear law of reduction of frequency. The nonlinear theory of the UHF amplifier is constructed on the basis of the chosen slowing down structure. The maximal amplitude of a longitudinal electrical field, the efficiency of interaction and the optimum length of the structure are determined.

articleTitle: High-power multibeam klystron with reversive magnetic focusing system
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)

articleTitle: Plasma electronics. Theoretical and experimental investigations of plasma nonlinearity in the traveling-wave tube oscillators
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Many years of plasma electronics development has led to powerful microwave devices creation. Due to use of plasma-filled electromagnetic structures these devices exhibit significant increase of efficiency, power and radiation bandwidth. Plasma-filled traveling-wave oscillators have been developed and studied. Special investigations of low frequency plasma oscillations, which appear in the powerful plasma-filled microwave devices, have been carried out. Such oscillations are one of the possible reasons for microwave generation pulse shortening. The usual premise of many investigations of beam-plasma instability is the assumption of independence of plasma parameters from microwave power. However various reasons for a dependence exist and the main are high frequency pressure (HFP) and high frequency discharge. Both these reasons lead to the appearance of a plasma longitudinal inhomogeneity. The resonance character of a beam-wave interaction makes it very sensitive to the inhomogeneity of the medium where the wave is propagated. Experiments are described which show that the role of HFP in increasing microwave power growth. It is confirmed by the large difference between plasma densities near the input and output ends of the system.

articleTitle: Frequency-step-tunable high-power gyrotron for plasma physics applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this work we discuss how to tune the frequency of a high-power gyrotron. The importance of this problem increases in the case of using gyrotrons in large-size fusion machines. The point is that the magnetic field in large stellarators and tokamaks considerably changes over the distance from the plasma center to its boarder. This means that the resonance condition between the plasma electrons and the gyrotron signal is fulfilled only in a relatively small layer of the plasma. To reach other plasma layers one must either use mechanically steerable mirrors to direct the RF wave to the desired position and to employ the Doppler shift effect, or change the frequency of the source and, hence, the position of the resonance layer in the plasma. It is quite obvious that the second possibility is more attractive, because it reduces the number of mechanically movable parts close to the plasma in a fusion machine and increases reliability of operation of the entire system.

articleTitle: Plasma electromagnetic generator as mean of direct plasma stream energy conversion to monochromatic microwave radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: One of the possible ways to generate microwave radiation with millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths is the direct conversion of plasma stream energy to monochromatic microwave radiation under braking of the plasma stream in a transverse magnetic field. We called this microwave system a "plasma electromagnetic generator", the abbreviation of which is PEMG.

articleTitle: Design and investigation of high-power helix TWT for systems of distant and space communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The application in output cascades of multichannel high-power transmitters of wideband vacuum devices, which are capable to work at several frequencies simultaneously, is an actual problem. The multifrequency modes were investigated in high-power helical TWT, having the band of amplified frequencies more than 40% and working without regulation of applied voltage in all operating frequency range. The third-order elements of the intermodulation products (3rd IMPE) were investigated by operation in a multifrequency mode at different levels of the output signal. For the purpose of getting a regular amplitude-frequency characteristic (AFC) and damping of self-excitation in a working mode, we used different parameters of the helix for the different parts of a slow-wave system (SWS) and optimum location of additional local attenuators.

articleTitle: High-power multiple-beam klystrode for UHF-band TV-transmitters
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: A relatively new device called the klystrode to be used in UHF-band TV-system transmitters appeared on the market in the 1990's. Owing to its high efficiency, linearity, reliability, and relatively low dimensions, klystrodes have come into wide use as high-power output amplifiers for UHF-band TV transmitters (470-860 MHz). The major manufacturer of klystrodes today is EEV. The promising features of klystrodes for TV-transmitters make designers search for new ways of improving their parameters. During 1995 to 1998, SRPC "ISTOK" experts using a 25-year experience of development and manufacture of microwave multiple-beam devices (klystrons and TWTs) created a new design of a high-power klystrode, i.e. a multiple-beam klystrode. The multiple-beam design opens up a new opportunity for further improvement of the klystrode parameters by reducing the operating voltage and increasing the total current.

articleTitle: Effective amplification of microwaves in structures with field and secondary emission
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: A new design of microwave distributed amplifier (DA) has been proposed, in which RF voltage is applied to anode-gate gap, FEA is a source of unmodulated current, anode is more negative than gate, and RF electron current is caused by secondary emission modulation from anode due to energy modulation of primary electrons. It is important that there is no RF voltage on FEA, so it's current can be strongly stabilized by resistive layer, and low transconductance and high microwave losses don't influence DA parameters. Preliminary analysis (neglecting space charge of secondary electrons) has shown that secondary electrons' flow ceases instantly if minimum of potential arises in anode gap at anode voltage varying during RF period. This corresponds to infinite transconductance. Therefore one can expect that real transconductance (accounting space charge) should have enormous value.

articleTitle: Ion explosive emission in microwave field
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In a microwave field at a liquid conducting surface, a super-small microrelief with a high field amplification factor can be produced. Field-electron and field-ion emission from this structure were initiated simultaneously at appropriate half-wave of the field as a stable phase and this process was limited only by the thermal balance at the emitter surface in the microwave field. This balanced mode can be shifted to an aperiodic stage both by static and microwave field but with different efficiency and results. The increase of microwave field does not lead to the uncontrollable filling of the resonator with emitter substance and a new mode of high-current ion emission is possible in this case. For the first time, it is experimentally shown that the field-ion emission in a microwave field can be transformed into a stable self-sustaining ion emission when the ion current is increased explosively by 2-3 orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of charged particles impinging on electrode in RF and microwave discharges
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The main goal of the present work is to measure electron and ion fluxes on electrodes in RF and microwave discharges, and to determine discharge parameters and the mechanism of high frequency field absorption. We designed secondary electron diagnostics in a low pressure capacitive RF discharge and measured the sheath voltage waveform and electron density in the plasma region. Also, we established ion flux diagnostics of microwave discharges in a magnetic field. We studied the exciting wave polarization influence on flux intensity of ions impinging on the substrate. The results allow us to determine experimentally the pressure range where the electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) power absorption mechanism dominates.

articleTitle: A computer code for solving nonstationary self-consistent consistent electromagnetic field and particle motion equations
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: A computer code for simulation of charged particle motion in nonstationary electromagnetic field is described. Electromagnetic field is excited by charged particle current density and (or) outer sources and is found in time domain by FDTD method in rectangular or cylindrical systems of coordinates. Outer constant electric and magnetic fields may be imposed as an initial condition. Charged particle motion is simulated by particle-in-cell (PIC) method. The code solves two-dimensional self consistent problems and is designated for personal computers with moderate resources and Windows 95/98/NT operational system.

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental study of helical electron beams in millimeter wave range powerful gyrotrons
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The basic properties of helical electron beams (HEB) formed in the magnetron-injection gun (MIG) of powerful multimeter wave range gyrotrons are investigated. Guns for 1 MW power level 83, 110, 140 and 170 GHz gyrotrons, forming quasilaminar, regularly intersecting, mixed and boundary (between quasilaminar and regularly intersecting) HEB are considered. Evolution of the electron oscillatory velocities distribution function has been traced. Influence of the reflected electrons on beam parameters are studied experimentally.

articleTitle: Slow-wave structure for high-power electron devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: One of the main features of slow-wave structures (SWS), intended for electromagnetic wave amplification or for the acceleration of electron beams, is the presence of a longitudinal electric field, with a relatively uniform distribution in the SWS cross-section. A new type of SWS corresponding to the mentioned requirement is presented in this work. The axially symmetric E-type electromagnetic wave is excited in a tube with a relative permeability /spl mu/ in the azimuth direction. The excited wave has the same components as the E/sub 01/ wave in a cylindrical waveguide and propagates along the magnetic tube with deceleration. The analysis has shown, that the field of the E/sub 01/ wave in a magnetic tube has a structure which is optimum for interaction with an electron beam. The creation in the future of a magnetic material with small electromagnetic losses will allow one to realize the proposed SWS for high-power devices.

articleTitle: On a class of singular points in solutions of dense electron beam equations
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Under hydrodynamic approximation components of electromagnetic field in projections on the axes of Lagrange's system of coordinates are represented by the law of motion of charged particles. Using inhomogeneous Maxwell's equations there can be got equations of dense electron beam which consists of the only law of motion and integrals of motion in projections on axes of Lagrange's system of coordinates.

articleTitle: Investigation of advanced coaxial gyrotrons at IAP RAS
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Some results of experimental testing of the 140 GHz/ 1,5 MW coaxial gyrotron (Russian version of the joint Russian-German coaxial gyrotron) with a lower level of ohmic losses in the cavity are presented and some nearest plans concerning the development of coaxial gyrotrons at IAP RAS are outlined. The report presents also the project of the future superpower coaxial gyrotrons with an acceptable (for CW-regime) level of the heat load density.

articleTitle: Regularized solution of Cauchy problem for Laplace equation regarding to electron optic systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Analysis of some electron optics systems, deduced to Cauchy problem for Laplace's equation which is noncorrect in classical sense is described. Regularized solution of the problem is found by two different methods and comparison of this methods is made.

articleTitle: Theory of multibeam electron-optical systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this work we discuss the calculational methods which exclude the brutal application on numerical algorithms in 3-space trajectory analysis programs for multibeam systems of interacting microstreams. There are the theory of non-relativistic system with large-scale ruling grid; the theory of relativistic injector with triode-type potential distribution at the axis in the absence of external magnetic field; the theory of one-layer relativistic systems in arbitrarily oriented magnetic field. The guaranteed accuracy of asymptotic theory and the probability of optimization due to variation of potential distribution distinguish this approach from 3-space numerical models which have all systematic shortcomings of 2-space programs so their accuracy can't be evaluated adequately.

articleTitle: The electrodynamics system for the multi-beam, broadband, continuously operating klystron with focusing system of plan symmetry and linear arrangement of the transit channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: During the last few decades in Russia broadband microwave amplifiers based on the multi-beam klystron with packed permanent magnet focusing system have gained a wide acceptance. The traditional arrangement of the transit channels with their centers to be located on the concentric circles has a substantial disadvantage-the complicated heat removal from the inner channel rows. This problem shows itself in the klystrons with packed reverse magnet system, where up to 20% of the electron flow power is deposited in the space of the last pole piece. The effective solution of this problem is to locate the transit channel centers in one or two linear rows; it means their linear arrangement. In this report the electrodynamics system (EDS) of the broad decimeter band klystron with transit channel linear arrangement and the output power up to some tens of kW in continuous operating regime is considered. The pole pieces of this klystron had rectangular form and the magnets are arranged over the long side of the pole pieces, so the reverse magnet focusing system (RMFS) was not axial but plane symmetric.

articleTitle: Processes in space charge of high-power microwave devices: Diagnostics and control
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Study of space-charge phenomena in high-power microwave devices is for a long time considered to be one of primary objectives of High-Current and Microwave Electronics Laboratory of St. Petersburg State Technical University. In our practice, we use various diagnostic methods including standard, generally accepted ones. Three of our original techniques will be characterized in this paper. These techniques had been developed to yield information on space charge distribution and collective effects in systems with magnetic confinement and on transverse (relative to magnetic field vector) components of electron velocity in magnetized flows.

articleTitle: Skin-current effects on particle production in ultra high frequency vacuum devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Operating of Ultra High Frequency Electron Vacuum Tubes (UHF EVT) could be essentially bound to intensive skin-currents on electrodes surfaces restricting working vacuum volume. It is known that thus the skin-current effect of fast desorption (FD) (previous than thermal) of positive or negatively ionized atoms and neutral as well from a surface of metal are possible. The receipt of the formed streams of particles in an interaction space and active working medium of the device could affect on properties of this medium and parameters of the device as a whole, and represents from this point of view considerable research interest. We represent here results of complex experimental research.

articleTitle: Plasma diagnostics in open resonator
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The methods and the results of weakly absorbing plasma investigation with the help of the two-mirror open resonator in the millimeter range are presented. The frequency of electron collisions with different particles and the electronic density of plasma in the flame of gas burners were measured. The accuracy of measurements and the scope for method used were determined.

articleTitle: Field analysis in multi-mode microwave heating chambers with several power inputs
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: One of the main problems while designing industrial installations for microwave processing of products is providing uniform heating of an object, which is determined by electromagnetic field distribution in a heating unit chamber. With a resonator of large size, also in order to increase field distribution uniformity in the volume of a working chamber, several power inputs positioned at a distance from each other are often used. The same method makes it possible to increase the rate of product heating and to enlarge the volume of a heated product. This work concerns development of programs for calculation and research of electromagnetic fields in multi-mode prismatic chambers designed for microwave heating.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation results for improving the magnetron injection gun in 8 mm wavelength gyrotron
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Some methods for improving the performances of magnetron injection gun of gyrotron, especially increasing the ratio of transverse to longitudinal velocity, are described in this paper. /spl alpha/=2.39 has been reached by modifying the magnetic field profile in adiabatic compression area, adjusting the equilibrium between electric field force and magnetic field force, and changing the tilt angle of the post focus pole. This value is much larger than the original value (/spl alpha/=1.4). Besides, the reversion, oscillation and interception of electron beam in the gun area can avoided by selecting gun parameters.

articleTitle: Stock's waves at conducting liquid surface in static and SHF electric fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Summary form only given. The problem of the description of nonlinear Stock's waves on the surface of a conducting liquid with an electrical field applied at the liquid-vacuum boundary is investigated. Mathematical model was developed that takes into account the effects of electric field in nonlinear approximation with any accuracy required. The ratio of the wave amplitude to its length was employed as a small parameter. Due to that the problem of the effects of electric field on the profile of an arbitrary two-dimensional surface wave could have been solved. Basing on these results, the problem of non-linear wave bifurcation from a zero level was solved. The existence of a Stock's wave is proved. The formula of approximating the profile of a wave and dispersion equation with the third order of accuracy is obtained. The influence of weak non-linearity to development of instability near to a threshold is investigated.

articleTitle: Rezotrod: opportunities of the solution of a problem of a uniform volumetric heating of large-sized objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: We present a new high-performance small-sized multi-beam device, called a rezotrod, for uniform volumetric heating of large-sized objects. It has the advantages of UHF devices (complete passage of a current, closed electrodynamics systems), and grid tubes (supply without modulation, small length electrostatic focusing). It also has its own distinctive advantages (stabilized amplitude of an UHF voltage in an output gap, independent generating contour).

articleTitle: Electrodynamic structure of two-beam induction accelerator
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Recently it has been proposed a new scheme of two beam induction accelerator. This scheme is based on RF acceleration of charged particles via an excitation of cavities by a self-bunching drive electron beam. This report presents a design of electrodynamic structures of the two-beam linac for an electron-positron linear collider and a heavy ion accelerator.

articleTitle: Vircator with delay feedback and beam modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In the present paper modification of vircator with preliminary beam modulation and additional delay feedback loop is studied by numerical simulation. It is shown that variance of delay time in the feedback leads to change of phase of modulation signal, what allows to drive the generation characteristics.

articleTitle: Resonance mechanism of operating frequency fixation in relativistic Cherenkov generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Electrodynamical systems (EDS) of open resonators that are widely used in modern experiments for microwave generation in the relativistic Cherenkov type devices consist of a diaphragm cut off neck, corrugated slow-wave structure (SWS) and a conical horn antenna. As a rule an axisymmetrical mode is an operating wave in such type of generators. In this paper numerical investigations of open resonators are made with help of computer codes based on linear theory for Cherenkov type devices.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of electron field emission from fractal surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Materials possessing significant emission ability in rather weak fields have great importance for vacuum microelectronics. From our point of view, the most realistic explanation of so low voltage required for emission, and its non-uniform character, can be given taking into account fractal structure of emitter surface. In other words, there are self-similar micro-irregularities on the emitter, on which repeated amplification of electrostatic field takes place. In this paper, we present a numerical simulation of electron emission from fractal surfaces.

articleTitle: Universal dielectric for creation of miniature UHF electronic devices anodic alumina
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The unique aluminum oxide technology and its product-anodic alumina (AA) substrates both with and without aluminum base-hold much promise for semiconductor and vacuum microelectronics applications. The basis for successful applications of AA as a ceramic dielectric in UHF electronics is their unique electrophysical properties, which are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Features of quasi-gasdynamic plasma confinement in ECR ion source with powerful microwave pumping
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Powerful ECR heating of a mirror-trapped plasma leads to formation of an anisotropic electron velocity distribution function (EDF): the average energy of the transverse, with respect to the magnetic field, electron motion is much greater than the energy of longitudinal motion. Theoretical studies of a mirror magnetic confinement of a multicomponent plasma with anisotropic EDF in a simple mirror trap reveals an essential augmentation in multicharged ion confinement time due to the EDF anisotropy. Consequently, the EDF anisotropy improves the ion charge state distribution (CSD). In this paper we discuss results of experimental investigation of an ECR discharge sustained by powerful pulse microwave radiation of a gyrotron in a mirror magnetic trap. In particular, data on plasma X-ray emission spectrum and on ion CSD are presented. Formation of the ion CSD has been explored both experimentally and numerically.

articleTitle: Radiation patterns formed by overmoded electrodynamic structures of relativistic Cerenkov generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)

articleTitle: Generation and amplification of electromagnetic radiation in the relativistic ubitrons with the over-cyclotron-resonance guiding magnetic field
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this work a method to generate long X-band pulses, based on stimulated emission of electrons moving in undulator fields, is studied. Note that a FEL operating at microwave frequencies is quite often referred as ubitron. Both the amplifier and the oscillator scheme of ubitron are tested. The experiments reported here represent the demonstration of operability of X-band ubitrons on the base of the accelerator "Saturn".

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of field enhancement factor for field emission cathodes with finite conductivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: We will consider here the influence of microscopic dimensions of field emitter array (FEA) components and their finite conductivity on RF electric field on the tip ending (and hence emission current). Several unusual effects exist in field emission structures at high frequencies, so we decompose our analysis into consideration of several model systems.

articleTitle: Recent developments of scientific instruments in Millimeter Wave Division of ELVA-1 Ltd
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The Millimeter Wave Division of ELVA-1 Ltd. specializes in the design of scientific instruments. In this report we present a few samples of instruments for scientific research like high temperature plasma diagnostics, diagnostics of high power mm-wave sources like gyrotrons and EPR spectrometers. The main parameters of instruments and principles of operation are presented as well as technical approaches used in instrument design. New millimeter wave technologies which allow one to achieve specifications of instruments are described.

articleTitle: Passive millimetre wave imaging and absorption from exhaust gases
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Passive millimetre wave imaging systems have been developed and their applications investigated at DERA Malvern for several years. In this paper the applications of passive millimetre wave imaging for the detection of exhaust gases is investigated. In principle, this is feasible over the whole of the millimetre wave band. DERA has developed the world's first mechanically scanning real-time passive millimetre wave imager for the Ka band, the lower frequency end of the millimetre wave band. Currently at W-band, DERA is developing a real time imager using MMIC electronics to build the compact focal plane receiver array. Recent developments in MMIC technologies are beginning to make possible development of real time passive millimetre wave imaging systems at the still higher frequencies of the F- and D-bands.

articleTitle: Influence of geometry on electromagnetic oscillation generation in the virtual cathode triode
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The triode with virtual cathode (VC) generates gigawatt pulses in a wide frequency band. Basically, existing theoretical investigations of this system were carried by method of numerical simulation and not did explain many experimental facts. The analytical description is more successful for description of generation mechanism. It allows one to find the main dependencies of frequency spectrum and generation efficiency on parameters of the VC triode and resonant system. It makes it possible to build high-efficiency devices.

articleTitle: Klystron design method based on "one-dimensional" models of electron beam
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The peculiarities of klystron design based on "one-dimensional" electron beam models are considered. Electron device design on the basis of programs with the one-dimensional approach to charged particles motion equation results from insufficient up-to-date personal computer rating. Use of such an approach propounds a question about the attainable model precision while the devices with assigned output parameters should be designed. Computer program "KLYS-4.5" (interface version 4 and mathematical models version 5) had been worked out at SRBC "Toriy" and has been exploited longer than five years. This program allows one to calculate output parameters and characteristics of single- and multi-beam klystrons, that can contain input and output multi-linked filter systems, with one- and two-gap cavities having resonance frequencies lying in the ranges of the first and the second input signal harmonics.

articleTitle: Works toward the creation of powerful pulse RF generators of the X-band
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this review basic results of the work on the creation of RF power supply source for the accelerator with Colliding Linear Electron-Positron Beams (Russian abbreviation-VLEPP) are presented. The work was performed over a period of more than 10 years by collectives of Budker INP lab in Novosibirsk and INP Branch in Protvino under the direction of V.E. Balakin. Part of the work was done in collaboration with JINR (Dubna). One of elaborated klystron versions was installed and successfully tested in KEK (Japan).

articleTitle: Radiative Pierce instability in plasma waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The majority of present-day high-power pulsed microwave sources are based on the resonant stimulated emission of microwaves by relativistic electron beams in various electromagnetic systems. One of these sources is the relativistic Cherenkov plasma microwave oscillator. However, the system able to confine the plasma for a long time is expensive. Alternative devices, nonresonant microwave oscillators based on the radiative Pierce instability are considered. Radiative Pierce instability develops in systems in which strong positive feedback occurs. This feature makes Pierce instability universal, unlike resonance instabilities (such as Cherenkov). The same feature does not allow the creation of amplifiers working with this effect, but allows a wide class of oscillators to be created. In plasma waveguides we can select at least three regimes of Pierce instability. If in the system the feedback is effected by beam potential wave then aperiodic instability occurs, which breaks beam current and doesn't produce radiation. Radiative instability arises if the feedback is affected by non-potential wave.

articleTitle: Study of chemical weapon agent disposal based on microwave energy application
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Discusses research work dealing with the effects microwaves exert on different substances, first of all, on chemical weapon agents (CWAs). The first stage of investigation included tests with a surrogate CWA and the results have shown that microwave energy at 2450 MHz is most effectively absorbed by organophosphorus agents (OPA). Tributylphosphate (TBP) was used as the surrogate CWA. The tests with TBP revealed that the substance was being disintegrated by microwave energy absorbed. The temperature of the agent was 270 to 3000/spl deg/C, while the temperature of the reactor's walls was 100/spl deg/C less. If ordinary incineration technology is used for destruction of chemical weapons, the shell has to be heated up to 600-7000/spl deg/C. These tests proved the high efficacy of the method, and the agent's residue upon completion of the process did not exceed 1/spl times/10/sup -4/. Energy consumption was 2 kWh per 1 kg of the agent.

articleTitle: On the simple model of electron beam with overcritical current [in vircators]
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this paper one of the simplest models of electron beam with overcritical current in the plain diode has been proposed. The behaviour of this model, called a "cellular conveyer", is coincident to the computation data of electron beams with overcritical current.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic theory of the radiative Pierce instability
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Nonresonance microwave sources based on the stimulated Pierce radiation of relativistic electron beams in smooth waveguides are presented. The microwave Pierce oscillator is a smooth cylindrical waveguide, along the axis of which a straightline relativistic electron beam propagates. To derive the growth rate of the radiative Pierce instability, the energy change of an electron propagating through the waveguide is calculated.

articleTitle: To calculation of TWT output characteristics outside the transparent band of coupled-cavities delay line sections
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: There are basically two factors that influence significantly the accordance between the computed results and the experimental data: strictness of the solution of the self-consistent problem of interaction of an electron beam with the high frequency field of the sections and accuracy of modeling the "cold" electrodynamical characteristics of the sections including terminal loads, where values can be determined by the known frequency dependences of the VSWR of the sections.

articleTitle: Beam-plasma amplifier on basis of coaxial transmission line
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The excitation of UHF-oscillations by an electron beam in a disk loaded coaxial transmission line with combs on the inner and external conductors are theoretically investigated. The structure passage channel, where an annular electron beam propagates, is fully filled by plasma. The eigen waves of the plasma filled coaxial transmission line and their dependencies versus plasma density are investigated. It is shown that the plasma has resulted in essentially an enhancement of gain and at the same time widens the excited oscillation spectrum.

articleTitle: Transmission of the infinite frequencies by using high-T/sub c/ superconductors: Part II: Experiments
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: This paper describes a "new formula" to provide the transmission of Ultra-High Frequencies (theoretically up to infinite) by using the High-T/sub c/ Superconductors. The "new formula" has experimentally been proved and justified. In addition, this paper deals with the enhancement of the Einstein's famous formula based on the "new formula". Please note that this paper has been splitted as two parts of a whole: "theoretical approach" and "experiments". This part (Part II) of the paper gives the information related to the experiments to prove and justify the "new formula" and consequently to enhance the Einstein's Famous Formula.

articleTitle: Generation of electromagnetic waves at anomalous Doppler effect. Experimental investigations and applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In this work, attention is paid to experimental investigations of the anomalous Doppler effect at the electron cyclotron frequency in systems consisting of an electron beam and a helical slow wave structure or interdigital periodic structure placed in a longitudinal resonance magnetic field. In this case slow cyclotron waves in the beam and eigenmodes in the structure can be excited. RF generation conditions are analysed and application to the development of an ion accelerator with RF field excitation is discussed.

articleTitle: A diagnostic setup for measurement of time-resolved electron beam distributions in high-power O-type devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Characteristics of a new all-in-one setup for experimental determination of electron beam parameters of high-power microwave O-type devices are given. The measurements were made in the collector part of the device, where the electron beam expanded in the absence of external electric or magnetic fields after interaction with the rf structure. The analyzing section was mounted to the microwave tube instead of the collector unit to measure spatial, angular and energy distributions of the electron beam.

articleTitle: The reflection influence at powerful gyrotron complex operation
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: Powerful gyrotrons are used for fusion plasma heating and current drive under ECR conditions in such devices as TOKAMAKs and STELLARATORs. Electrodynamic system of gyrotrons and microwave transmitting lines may contain different types of reflections of microwave power from line components, dielectric windows, chamber walls, etc. The reflected signal gets into operating volume of gyrotron cavity changing the conditions of electron beam interaction with RF field. The dependencies of output parameters on reflection coefficient and delay time were investigated. Estimation of the conditions for oscillation stability and enhancement of output signal spectrum in the presence of a reflected signal is given.

articleTitle: Application of the generalized eigenvalue method to the theory of the waveguide partially filled with the dissipative dielectric
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The problem of wave propagation through a waveguide partially filled with lossy dielectric has been a subject of interest for several years due to its practical importance. However, a good solution to this problem is not achieved in the general case because of the mathematical difficulties caused by the radiation condition which is enforced at an infinite distance from the exciting sources. In the present work we leave out the radiation condition and intend to use the bounded absorption principle together with the generalized eigenvalue method. The latter is adopted in some points in order to apply it to infinite waveguides. The approach we used is based on two ideas which are as follows: a) the original infinite lossy waveguide boundary problem may be replaced by a finite short-circuited waveguide i.e. resonator boundary problem. b) The electromagnetic field excited may be treated as an analytical function of the slab's dielectric constant and can be computed by means of the analytical expansion.

articleTitle: Experimental studies of dense electron beam transport through diaphragms
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The situation when an electron beam is transported through a system of diaphragms or a channel with transverse dimensions close to those of the beam is typical for electron-beam vacuum microwave devices. Inner surfaces of the channel or diaphragms are subjected to bombardment with particles of the beam halo. In high-power devices, this bombardment may cause non-linear phenomena having a substantial effect on transportation of the main part of the beam. We present data on processes similar to those found in developing electron-beam microwave devices with high electron beam parameters. We demonstrate the possibility of a critical influence of complicated phenomena, including generation of secondary particles and plasmas and non-linear collective oscillations, on the transport of a high-power electron beam. The investigations are performed for a broad range of conditions (beam current, energy deposition density on the electrodes surrounding the beam, etc.) and show a universality of the observed phenomena.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of transient electromagnetic field. State-of-art
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The main fields of FDTD method application are discussed, as follows: Antenna simulation and design, calculation of near-zone and far zone fields; scattering of electromagnetic waves and calculating RCS pattern; microwave circuit simulation; optoelectronic devices and optical fiber simulation; microwave power electron devices and accelerator analysis; plasma analysis; solving of biomedical problems and calculation of SAR patterns; and identification of hidden objects in water and soil.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the dynamic processes in the gyrotron adiabatic trap
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The output parameters of CW and quasi-CW gyrotrons are to a considerable extent defined by the quality of helical electron beams (HEBs) produced by magnetron-injection guns (MIGs). The characteristic feature of MIGs is the trapped magnetic field distribution and therefore some of electrons with greatest oscillatory velocities are reflected from the magnetic mirror and then are locked into the adiabatic trap between the cathode and cavity. According to the recent experimental data trapped electrons render the essential influence upon beam parameters that in particular causes the necessity to reduce the share of the oscillatory energy t/sub /spl perp// in the beam for conservation of its stability. Decreasing of t/sub /spl perp// leads to reducing the output gyrotrons efficiency. These facts denote necessity further perfection of the theoretical model of HEB first of all by taking into account the electrons reflected from the magnetic mirror. In this paper the results of numerical simulation of relaxation processes in MIGs working in subcritical regime and forming regularly intersecting, boundary and quasilaminar beams are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of coaxial mounting and probe structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: An efficient full-wave spectral domain analysis based on the integral equation method is developed for coaxial mounting and probe structure of a general form. Using this method, the algorithm for the complex input gap impedance of such structures has been derived and the calculated data are presented. The method may be useful for designing active and passive devices and probes mounted in a coaxial line.

articleTitle: Coupled slow-wave structures analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The author shows that the deceleration of an anti-phase electromagnetic wave in coupled slow-wave structures (CSWS) can exceed the so-called geometric deceleration many times. This can be used for resonant frequency decrease and energy concentration increase. It is also shown that the electric energy and magnetic energy can be split between different regions of a CSWS. In addition to the conventional application as a non-contact input and output in microwave vacuum amplifiers, the CSWS application as electrodes can be very effective in vacuum microelectronic devices with a distributed cathode.

articleTitle: Waves in electron beams-physical experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: In extended intensive electron beams it is possible to get excitation and spreading waves of different types. Of all the wave types the most important are the waves of space charge. Their investigation is of great interest both in practical application (microwave devices, wave methods of ion collective acceleration and others) and in study of fundamental problems, such as instability in beams of charged particles. In this work the results of physical experiment, devoted to investigation of linear and nonlinear waves of space charge in extended electric beams, drifting in longitudinal magnetic field are given. The physical experiment determines the spheres of application of different models used for description of waves in electron beams.

articleTitle: Dynamical chaos in the systems interaction of charged particles (computer simulations and experiment)
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The investigations of noise-like oscillating processes in intensive electron beams, due to the presence of virtual cathodes (VC), have been producing great interest. The forming of oscillating VC in beams of charges is a complex process in which the nonlinear behavior of space charge is displayed. The difficulties of describing such systems exists due to the processes of intensive interaction between the electron beam collecting degree of freedom and developed space charge. The examining system consists of two grids (O-type diode). On the first grid the unmodulated monospeed beam is featured. The ability of creating behavior of acceleration or braking exists through the different second grid potential supply. Virtual cathode was developed by the effect of space charge.

articleTitle: Technological gyrotrons with permanent magnet system
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The fulfillment of the new project of creation of the industrial prototype of a technological gyrotron on permanent magnets are discussed. The permanent magnet system was designed, constructed and successfully tested for a gyrotron. A 30 GHz gyrotron (n=2) with rf-output power of 10 kW is under development with the TE/sub 12/ operating mode. An output power of 12 kW was obtained (efficiency 24%).

articleTitle: Dissipative canonical nonuniform transmission lines as basic components of power dividers with distributed isolation impedance
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: It is well known that power dividers (PD) on nonuniform transmission lines (NUTL) with distributed isolation theoretically have no upper boundary of the operating frequency range in a single-wave approximation. This allows one to solve the problem of creating superwide-band microwave power divider in a natural way. For computation of such devices it is necessary to know the matrix parameter of the NUTL sections which, as it is known, can be found by solving linear differential equations of the second order with variable coefficients. Such solutions have been found for some types of NUTLs. However, they may not be applied to the computation of a power divider with distributed isolation since they have been obtained for loss-less lines. Therefore another computation method has gained acceptance: nonuniform lines are being replaced by cascade connection of stepped uniform transmission lines (UTL), and the distributed isolation impedance is replaced by the lumped one within each step. This method, being universal, has a number of drawbacks. A new type of NUTL namely the canonical nonuniform transmission line (CNUTL) has been suggested. The impedance function of CNUTL depends on two real parameters, and for their reasonably definite numerical values it assumes specific form which correspond to exponential, parabolic, hyperbolic, cosine-, sine-square, and other lines widely used in microwave engineering. This work is aimed at the generalization of the theory of the canonical nonuniform transmission lines for the case of dissipative lines and the study of their potential as structural elements of power dividers with distributed isolation impedance.

articleTitle: Analysis of multibeam magnetic focusing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The multibeam electron flows are used in microwave tubes, such as klystrons and traveling wave tubes. Their application allows to improve operational parameters, to increase a output power without increasing of accelerating voltage, to expand a frequency pass band. For focusing of such flows the magnetic systems with a uniform or reversal fields can be used. Peculiarities of multibeam flow focusing in such systems is connected with transverse components of magnetic field originating in peripheral channels.

articleTitle: Efficiency of energy recovery multistage systems in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: Proceedings International University Conference 'Electronics and Radiophysics of Ultra-High Frequencies' (Cat. No.99EX356)
abstract: The efficiency estimates of multistage electron energy recovery systems are important for gyrotrons operated at the first and second cyclotron harmonics. The development of multistage energy recovery systems requires knowledge of the electron energy spectra F(W) after the interaction with RF field. In this paper the numerical calculation of F(W) was carried out by the method of big particles on the basis of theory of gyrotron with non-fixed RF field structure taking into account the electron oscillatory velocity spread. Gaussian function of oscillatory velocity distribution at the working space entrance was used.
